name: passive_soi_ring_resonator
description: Pinned generic-PDK single-bus ring resonator from Section 3.6 of the FDTD-solver comparison paper and its supplementary repository.

oracle.reference: Zhu et al., arXiv:2506.16665v3, Section 3.6, Figure 26, and JPPhotonics/fdtd-pipeline at revision 622e0a9b7429eaf2335b1000b39e283544a198c4

layer_stack_reference.z_reference: Layer zmin values are measured from the shared silicon substrate plane at z=0 um

simulation.frequency_sampling: 101 uniform frequency samples between c / wavelength_stop and c / wavelength_start, matching projects/FDTD_solvers/ring/ring.py.
simulation.resolution_m_basis: The top-level resolution_m is the supplementary ring project default of 6 cells per wavelength in silicon at 1550 nm.
simulation.grid: BeamZ GridSpec.auto with the requested minimum cells per wavelength and a 1.4 maximum adjacent-cell scale.
simulation.subpixel: BeamZ diagonal Farjadpour interface averaging; the reference Tidy3D setup uses ContourPathAveraging.
simulation.source_time: Gaussian pulse with fwidth equal to the 20 nm simulated frequency span.
simulation.source_offset: Tidy3D default: 5 temporal widths; BeamZ equivalent: 5 / (2 pi).
simulation.beamz_boundary: A 1 um physical graded-conductivity absorber on every side.
simulation.run_time_rule: 30 * domain_x * 2 / c, matching the upstream Lumerical silicon path selected by projects/FDTD_solvers/ring/ring.py; the upstream Tidy3D helper uses 15
simulation.auto_shutoff: BeamZ field-energy decay threshold 1e-5 with the configured run time as a hard upper bound.
simulation.material_model_limitation: BeamZ uses nondispersive silicon and silica evaluated at 1550 nm; the supplementary solvers use fitted dispersive models.

published_ring_results.source: Zhu et al., arXiv:2506.16665v3, Section 3.6 and Figure 26
published_ring_results.metric: The lowest resonance in the 20 nm band after cubic interpolation from 0.2 nm monitor samples to approximately 0.02 nm; FWHM is measured at half depth and Q = resonance wavelength / FWHM.
published_ring_results.figure_26_digitization_note: Figure 26 provides the full per-resolution series graphically but the repository does not commit its raw solver arrays. Values other than those stated in the paper text must be treated as digitized approximations, not exact acceptance bounds.

six_ppw_acceptance.basis: Range spanning the two solvers at 6 PPW using values stated in the paper text; the Tidy3D FWHM upper endpoint is conservative because the text reports only its 0.88-0.90 nm range.

simulation.reference_result_limitation: The paper publishes ring comparisons in Figure 26 and text, but the supplementary repository does not commit the raw solver arrays. Six PPW is a published comparison point; the paper concludes that the ring requires 20 PPW for mesh convergence.
